context.situation: I direct a small arts and health charity delivering a three-year funded programme with one delivery partner. Funding is tightening and we must cut roughly 20%. The partner has twice written to our steering group raising concerns about how delivery decisions are made. Their delivery is adequate but not exceptional. Removing them would close the budget gap in one step and simplify governance. I am concerned about the wider relationship — they are well regarded in the community we work in — but I think the complaints indicate someone who is difficult to work with.
context.whatMatters: Keeping the programme financially viable and governable.
context.stakeholders: Charity, delivery partner, funder, programme participants, community.
context.uncertainties: Whether the governance complaints are substantive; effect of removal on community relationships.

evidence.text: Funding requires a cut of roughly 20%.
The partner has written to the steering group twice raising concerns.
I read the letters as indicating someone difficult to work with.
Their delivery is adequate but not exceptional.
Removing them closes the budget gap in a single step.
They are well regarded in the community we serve.
Concerns were routed to the steering group rather than the delivery team.
